hook_text: Switch on the kettle, the toaster and the microwave together and the kitchen goes dark. Here is the maths.
clip_script: Every light and plug in your home is wired in parallel. That means every appliance gets the full 230 volts, you can switch each one on by itself, and when one bulb blows the rest stay on. But because they all get the same voltage, the current each one draws depends on its resistance. Low resistance, big current. The thirstiest are the heaters: a kettle element of about 26 ohms gulps nearly 9 amperes, while an LED bulb sips about 0,04. And in parallel, currents add. Kettle: 8,7 amperes. Add the toaster: 12,2. Add the microwave: 17,4. On a 16 ampere kitchen circuit, click, the breaker trips. That click is a lifesaver, because too much current heats the wires until the plastic can melt and start a fire. So go easy on the multiplug, and switch on heavy appliances one at a time after load shedding.
visual_style: A kitchen with appliances lighting up one by one and a current counter climbing; a distribution board breaker flipping off; a glowing overloaded multiplug.
pacing: Everyday hook, quick rules, a climbing counter with suspense, then the click.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the rating plates on your appliances.
